children: Bank of England Deputy Governor Dave Ramsden said the impact of the central bank's quantitative tightening programme remained "very much in the background" in terms of raising yields in the British government bond market.

"Our principles are all about being gradual and predictable and QT operating in the background and Bank Rate being our primary tool," Ramsden told lawmakers from parliament's Treasury Committee on Thursday.
The BoE's Monetary Policy Committee is due to hold an annual vote on the pace of QT next week.

Ramsden cited analysis showing that QT — or the process of reducing the BoE's stock of gilts through a combination of active sales and allowing the bonds to mature without being reinvested — had raised yields by 20 to 30 basis points.
"In the context of a 200 basis point increase in term premia, I would argue (that) is still very much in the background," Ramsden said.
